topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the key learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Etiological Frameworks and the Origins of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual basis of cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease shaped by the interplay between endogenous mutational processes, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents and chronic infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma and Epstein-Barr virus as an illustrative case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical, Physical, and Promotional Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which environmental mutagens, metabolic activation, tumor promoters, and host developmental stages induce neoplastic transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and assess whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by synthesizing the primary themes of environmental cancer causation and discussing the everyday appraisal of exposure risks versus benefits.
